text:
The scoreboard said a rout, but the chances said NJD should have been the team still skating off with a point. NJD out-chanced NYI 4.05 to 3.63 in expected goals, fired 72 shot attempts to 50, and by the deserved-to-win measure took 56 percent of simulated replays. The difference was Ilya Sorokin, who stopped all 37 shots and saved 4.05 goals more than the chances against him should have allowed.

The game turned in the second period. NJD controlled it 2.24 to 1.49 in expected goals, and Jack Hughes had a 33 percent look that Sorokin turned away. NYI scored on three of their shots anyway: Simon Holmstrom at 3:32, Brayden Schenn at 5:00, and Bo Horvat on the power play at 12:08. Schenn's snap shot was the best of the three, a 30 percent chance, and he finished with a goal and an assist. Nico Daws, who saw 32 shots, ended up 2.37 goals worse than expected.

The third period turned a tight game into a lopsided one. Victor Eklund scored at 11:32 and Ondrej Palat followed 42 seconds later at 12:14, and Casey Cizikas added a short-handed goal at 18:41 to make it 6-0. NJD went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 0.69 expected goals there, while NYI went 1 for 3 and also scored once short-handed. NYI also won 28 of 49 faceoffs, 25 hits to 15, and 9 takeaways to 3. Matthew Schaefer, on the ice for 1.85 expected goals for and 0.76 against, assisted on two goals.
